assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and the dynamic amplification of shocks through credit are a core mechanism in modern macroeconomics. The framework underlies much of the post-2008 literature on financial frictions and is also a clean theoretical contribution.
assessment.attribution: Credit Cycles (1997) is a clear two-author contribution. Gertler and Gilchrist are important in the related financial-accelerator and empirical strand, but that strand overlaps with the work recognised in 2022, so I would not add them here.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of citation, extension and use in policy models. The core contribution is well confirmed.
uncertainties: The committee may judge the financial-frictions area partly covered by the 2022 prize.
Whether Gertler should be included depends on how the committee weighs the financial-accelerator lineage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offers bargaining with a unique subgame-perfect equilibrium is a foundational result in game theory. Its extension to decentralised markets links bargaining to search and market microstructure and shaped the later theory of matching and trading frictions.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the central contribution. Rubinstein and Wolinsky (1985) carry the market extension. Binmore's work on the strategic approach is substantial but secondary to the originating results, and Ståhl's earlier finite-horizon results precede them.
assessment.maturity: More than forty years of confirmation, with the model now standard in textbooks and applied theory. It is overdue on timing grounds.
uncertainties: The committee could prefer to credit Rubinstein alone or to add Binmore.
Game-theory prizes were awarded in 1994, 2005 and 2020, which may affect field balance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting reshaped international trade theory. The framework changed how gains from trade are understood and measured, and it links closely to micro-data work on firms.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the key model. Helpman's earlier monopolistic-competition trade theory and the Helpman–Melitz–Yeaple work on exports versus FDI are strongly linked to it. Redding's contributions are important but more recent and more quantitative.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of heavy empirical and theoretical follow-up, and the framework is now a workhorse.
uncertainties: Krugman received the 2008 prize for trade theory, so the committee may see the area as partly covered.
Helpman also appears in B020 under a separate discovery, which may complicate how his contributions are bundled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural estimation of differentiated-product demand and of dynamic industry models made empirical industrial organisation quantitative. It supports merger evaluation, competition policy and the measurement of market power.
assessment.attribution: The BLP demand framework (Berry; Berry–Levinsohn–Pakes) and the Ericson–Pakes dynamic framework are clearly identifiable. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are significant but less central to these specific methods, and credit is spread across a long list.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use in academia, antitrust agencies and industry. The contribution is well confirmed.
uncertainties: The list of credited names is long, and it is unclear who a committee would place in a group of up to three.
Bresnahan's contributions to the new empirical IO could be weighed against Berry's.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities and the New Keynesian framework underpin modern central-bank practice. The policy-rule and staggered-pricing tradition is highly influential in both theory and practice.
assessment.attribution: Calvo's staggered pricing, Taylor's rules and staggered contracts, and Woodford's synthesis are the clearest individual threads. The candidate credits eight people, including Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets, so any three-person selection leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Decades of integration into policy models and practice, so the work is mature.
uncertainties: Attribution is diffuse, and choosing three names is contestable.
Macroeconomics and monetary policy were recognised in 2004, 2011 and 2022, which may affect field balance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The long-run top-income series and the empirical reframing of inequality changed both research and public debate. The data-construction contribution is lasting. Some interpretive and theoretical claims remain disputed.
assessment.attribution: The Piketty–Saez top-income series is the core contribution. Zucman's work on wealth and offshore wealth is substantial but later and more contested in measurement.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of influence, with ongoing debate over measurement and interpretation.
uncertainties: Some committee members may weigh data and measurement against theoretical depth.
Methodological disputes over wealth-inequality estimates are ongoing.
Saez also appears in B044, and the committee may prefer to credit his work there.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based approach to technology and the race between education and technology explain wage inequality and job polarisation. Trade-shock studies add credible causal evidence on adjustment costs.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Katz and colleagues carry the skill-bias and task-polarisation work. Dorn and Hanson are central to the China-shock evidence, and Autor links both strands. Acemoglu's complementary task-based contributions were part of the 2024 prize context, and he is not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of replication and extension. The China-shock literature is still debated in its interpretation.
uncertainties: The recent 2024 prize may bear on how the committee sees technology and inequality.
Whether the committee prefers to combine technology and trade-shock strands or choose one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design give a general framework for how a sender can shape beliefs through information structures. It is conceptually clean, has already influenced theory, and has growing applications in market and mechanism design.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow (2011) is the originating contribution. Bergemann and Morris contributed the Bayes correlated equilibrium and a general information-design perspective. Credit is shared among two closely related strands.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years or so is short for this prize. Influence is strong in theory, but empirical and applied confirmation is still building.
uncertainties: The work may be too recent, and the committee may prefer to wait.
The choice of three names among four credited, and between the persuasion and information-design strands, is uncertain.
